title: Decision explainer — plugin resolution and the working-attitude mandate

masthead.headline: Three decisions this repository already rests on, explained for someone who was not there when they were made.
masthead.lede: Each section tells the story a decision answered, what was chosen in plain words, what else was on the table, and what it changes about your own work. Nothing here asks you to agree: leave a decision on “I'm good with it”, or press “Tell me more about it” and say what is still unclear.

sections.label: ADR-1 · Plugin resolution
sections.title: A hook finds the plugins it depends on by asking, never by guessing a folder.

points.lead: Every plugin carries an identical copy of one lookup command.
text: A hook runs its own
and gets back the folder Essential is installed in, or a failure.
Picture the moment a session starts in the Coding plugin. Its

text.definition: a command a harness runs by itself when something happens

text: has to run a script that belongs to a different plugin, Essential. Coding knows where it is installed itself — the harness tells it — but nobody tells it where Essential is. Claude Code keeps a registry of install locations, Codex keeps versioned caches, and Grok Build may run a copy laid out like this repository. A hook that assumed “Essential sits next door, at
” would work on one machine, miss on the next, and on a third quietly run an old copy from somewhere else.

blocks.title: What happens when Coding's session-start hook needs Essential
blocks.source:
flowchart TD
  H[Coding hook starts] --> R[Run Coding's own scripts/plugin-root essential]
  R --> D{Which harness set its root variable?}
  D -->|PLUGIN_ROOT| X[Codex: same marketplace cache, same version preferred]
  D -->|GROK_PLUGIN_ROOT| G[Grok Build: marketplace laid out like the source]
  D -->|CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT| C[Claude Code: installed_plugins.json registry]
  X --> M{Candidate's manifest names essential?}
  G --> M
  C --> M
  M -->|yes| P[Print the folder and exit 0]
  M -->|no, missing, or ambiguous| F[Print nothing and exit 1]
  P --> S[Hook runs essential/scripts/...]
  F --> E[Hook stops with an error instead of guessing]
blocks.alt: Coding's hook runs its own copy of scripts/plugin-root with the name essential. The resolver checks which harness variable is set — PLUGIN_ROOT for Codex, GROK_PLUGIN_ROOT for Grok Build, CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT for Claude Code — and looks in that harness's own install records. A candidate is accepted only if its manifest names essential; then the folder is printed and the hook runs Essential's script. Otherwise nothing is printed, the resolver exits 1, and the hook stops with an error.

blocks.text: The choice, in plain words: one lookup command is written once, at the root of the repository, and copied unchanged into every plugin. A hook only ever runs the copy inside its own plugin, so it never reaches outside its own folder to find the tool that finds everything else. This command is the one file the repository allows to exist in more than one plugin; everything else shared has a single owner.

comments.text: The whole decision is this line: ask the plugin's own resolver, and stop loudly if it cannot answer.

text: The one alternative the record weighs is the guess itself: work out Essential's folder from Coding's own. It was rejected because the three harnesses lay plugins out differently, so a guessed path either misses Essential or finds an unrelated copy. The price of the chosen design is small and stated: every plugin carries the same short file, and the copy step has to be kept current.

sections.label: L1 · Working attitude stays global
sections.title: Every agent is still told to read the working-attitude file, even when it is not writing code.

points.lead: A proposal to save one file read was turned down.
points.text: The file's guidance applies to all work, not only code, so hiding it from non-coding sessions would cost more than the read it saves.
